chunks: 2409 - Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said:
"Whoever goes out on a journey while carrying a staff of bitter almond wood and recites this verse:
"And when he turned himself toward Madyan, he said: Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way."
up to the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"And Allah is Trustee over what we say."

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will keep him safe from every harmful beast, every hostile thief, and every venomous creature until he returns to his family and his home; and there will be with him seventy-seven of the attendant angels seeking forgiveness for him until he returns and sets it down."

key_terms.الْآيَةَ: the Qur’anic verse to be recited
key_terms.الْمُعَقِّبَاتِ: attendant angels who follow and guard

ai.seo_question: What should be recited for protection during travel according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a travel practice taught by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم: carrying a bitter almond staff and reciting verses connected to Prophet Musa’s journey and trust in divine guidance. Its significance is the promise of Allah’s protection during travel and the companionship of angels seeking forgiveness for the traveler.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2409 - Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said that the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings of Allah (swt) be upon him and his family) said:
"Whoever embarks on a journey and carries with them a bitter almond stick, and recites this verse:
'When he directed himself toward Madyan, he said, "Perhaps my Lord (azj) will guide me to the right way."'
up to the words of Allah (swt),
'And Allah (swt) is a witness over what we say.' (Surah Al-Qasas 28:22-28),

Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious, will protect them from every harmful beast, every aggressive thief, and every venomous creature until they return to their family and home. Additionally, seventy-seven angels will accompany them, seeking forgiveness for them until they return and set it (the stick) down."
